definition: Eclectic means made up of a diverse variety of elements or styles drawn from many different sources.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word eclectic. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know eclectic should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Professor Nguyen's reading list was famously eclectic, pairing ancient poetry with detective stories, science essays, and graphic memoirs from around the world.
A varied collection simply includes different kinds of things, while an eclectic one deliberately gathers its pieces from many separate sources and styles.
An eclectic collector chooses favorites from many traditions, but an encyclopedic one tries to cover every tradition there is.

Wide-ranging measures breadth: a wide-ranging survey or conversation covers many areas and topics. Eclectic is about where the pieces come from — an eclectic collection is deliberately drawn from many separate sources, styles, or traditions, chosen because the mix itself is the point.

Multifaceted describes a single thing with many different sides or aspects, like a multifaceted problem or career. Eclectic describes a collection assembled from many separate sources and styles; the variety lies in where its pieces were drawn from, not in the facets of one thing.

Diverse says a group contains many different kinds, and it describes the result no matter how it came about. Eclectic emphasizes the choosing: an eclectic mix was deliberately selected from many separate sources or traditions by someone's own taste.
